title: Feature tags
key_points: Godot has a special system to tag availability of features.

Each feature is represented as a string, which can refer to many things like platform name, architecture, type, supported texture compression algorithms, debug or release build, running from the editor or standalone binary, and more.
Features can be queried at runtime by calling OS.has_feature(name).
OS feature tags are used by GDExtension to determine which libraries to load.
There are default features, custom features, and features can be overridden in Project Settings.
limitations: With the exception of texture compression, web_<platform> and movie feature tags, default feature tags are immutable.
Custom feature tags are not used when running a project from the editor, even if the export preset is marked as Runnable for your current platform.
To check whether a project exported to Web is running on a mobile device, use OS.has_feature("web_android") or OS.has_feature("web_ios")).
asserts: Godot provides a system of feature tags to represent the availability of features in different runtime conditions.
scope: The main thrust applies to developers using Godot and exporting their projects for different platforms, architectures, and configurations.
